domain_model: Uses paired boundary correspondence from the locked Phase 2.36f centerline, leftBoundary, and rightBoundary polylines. Each side is normalized from carrier u=0 to boundary u=1. Topology samples are over normalized side-domain, not degrees or half-degree rings.
geometry_source: Phase 2.36f HTML DATA payload; centerline/leftBoundary/rightBoundary/polygon copied unchanged
rendering_method: SVG vector overlay. No raster ImageData field, no blur, no gaussian feather, no canvas composited wash. Semi-transparent vector strokes/polygons are used only as structural topology marks.

visual_assessment.asc_read: ASC benefits from paired boundary correspondence and vector topology; carrier reads more stable than the alpha-wash studies.
visual_assessment.mc_read: Compressed contour and hybrid modes read most topographic; terrace mode is useful but can become too graphic.
visual_assessment.recommended_next_pass: Tune structural density and carrier/field contrast. Explore fewer, more intentional contour samples before any production discussion.
risks: May overcorrect into diagrammatic contour-map language.
Visible structural marks may compete with map labels at smaller scales.
Terraces must not be mistaken for degree bands; report labels them visual topology samples only.

visual_thesis: A pressure field may need organized topology: contour compression, terraces, vector strip organization, directional laminations, and density rhythm around an exact carrier ridge rather than a continuous alpha fog.
why_phase_238_insufficient: Phase 2.38 replaced per-pixel raster pressure with boundary-parametric quads, but the visual transfer still used transparent blue area accumulation. It remained perceptually close to blur paint: dark carrier, soft wash, fade-out. The failure was structural organization, not banding.
